answer: Sybil resistance here is geological. Reputation accumulates like basalt, layer by cooled layer, one epoch at a time, and no attacker can fake strata that took months to harden. An oasis is cheap to claim but expensive to hold: presence, attestations and graded work must all be renewed every close, so cloning identities multiplies the cost instead of the reward. Ferrous traces left in each signed record bind it to real elapsed time, which is the one resource a fork cannot mint.
